You're correcting zoom-in shot targeting for a screen-recording video edit. A previous pass got several targets WRONG, and the user (who watched the actual render) flagged specific problems. Your job: re-verify every zoom target against real frames (you have vision — use it, don't guess), fix what's wrong, and be conservative about zoom tightness.

SOURCE: `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\screen.mp4`, 1920x1080, 60fps. Grab frames with (Git Bash, PATH already includes ffmpeg after this): `export PATH="/c/Users/edmem/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/Gyan.FFmpeg_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/ffmpeg-9.0-full_build/bin:$PATH"` then `ffmpeg -y -ss <seconds> -i screen.mp4 -frames:v 1 out.png`, then Read the PNG. **Sample densely — every 1-2 seconds within each window, not every 3-5s** — sparse sampling is exactly what caused the previous errors.

CRITICAL CONTEXT — a confirmed bug pattern: for a large stretch of this recording (roughly 553s onward), the screen is a SPLIT LAYOUT: a browser showing the "Codely" website on the LEFT (~x=0-1010), and a Claude-Code-style AI chat/agent panel on the RIGHT (~x=1010-1920, dark theme, scrolling conversation log, with a text input box near the bottom of that right panel, roughly y=1015-1060, where Nick's spoken words appear live via voice-to-text as he dictates a prompt). The previous pass wrongly zoomed into the LEFT browser panel during moments when the actual focus was the LIVE VOICE-TO-TEXT TYPING happening in the RIGHT panel's input box. Confirmed concretely at source time ~744-759s: frames show text appearing keystroke-by-keystroke in the right panel's input box ("As soon as", then "As soon as I get onto the website, there", then the full sentence) — this is the "voice to text prompt into Claude" the user is referring to. Whenever the transcript has Nick narrating something that matches text visibly appearing in that right-panel input box, THAT input box is the correct zoom target, not the left browser. Check every window against this pattern, not just the one at 744-759s — the user said "there's a few of these instances."

OTHER FEEDBACK TO APPLY:
- Zoom levels have been going too tight in multiple spots, softening/degrading the image. Cap zoom factor at ~2.0-2.2x max (previous pass went up to 3.2x). Prefer a looser frame around the target over a tight crop — err toward showing more context, not less.
- (A separate technical fix for end-of-zoom jitter has already been made — you don't need to worry about that, only about WHAT each zoom targets and how tight it is.)

FULL TRANSCRIPT for context (phrase-level, seconds):
[399.85-444.05] Now I don't want to waste any more time, I would love to start working on Codely here... for some reason this website is very narrow like the margins are extremely narrow so I definitely think we need to change that. Obviously we need to take this out. This section is boring.
[446.83-454.23] this little animation here, and this stuff here definitely has to go.
[469.23-501.25] ...I want to use some inspiration from Google Gemini... it's got that nice illuminating glow around in the backgrounds so let's go ahead and try to emulate what Google Gemini has on the home page of Codely.
[553.45-593.29] So I have my prompt typed in and I've already hit enter... we're going to add this prompt box here on the home page of the website...
[622.34-674.56] ...as you could see we have the warm pink gradient... we did a warm pink gradient from pink peach to a little bit of magenta.
[675.14-694.44] And so this is the current logo that I have for Codely...
[708.08-718.16] Okay so obviously we have our first bug here as soon as you refresh the page it has this glow and then it just immediately fades away so we need to fix that.
[744.57-783.31] As soon as I get on to the website there is that illuminating glow around the chat box which is very vibrant and I think it's a little too opaque... a few seconds of loading the website the glow immediately disappears so it needs to be static and pulsating in the background behind the prompt chat box.

CURRENT (POSSIBLY WRONG) ZOOM CONFIG to re-verify, one by one, by looking at real frames across each full window — for each, confirm or correct the crop region, and confirm or correct the zoom timing:
1. window ~439.5-444.05: crop center (950,660), zoom 2.6 — target: the specific called-out section (browser text-selection highlight) during "obviously we need to take this out, this section is boring"
2. window ~448.0-454.23: crop center (954,813), zoom 3.0 — target: "this little animation" carousel/highlighted section
3. window ~484.5-494.5 (within clip 469.23-501.25): crop center (970,580), zoom 2.3 — supposedly the real Google Gemini website tab
4. window ~658-674.56 (within clip 636.05-674.68): crop center (455,455), zoom 3.2 — pink gradient button — RECHECK, this zoom is too tight (3.2x), loosen it
5. window ~676-694.44 (within clip 675.09-694.56): crop center (1087,572), zoom 2.4 — the logo
6. window ~708.03-717 (within clip 708.03-718.28): crop center (490,495), zoom 2.6 — the bug: glow appearing then fading on refresh — RECHECK whether this is on the left browser or could involve the right panel too
7. window spanning 744.52-783.43 (two separate kept ranges: 744.52-759.51 and 769.30-783.43): crop center (475,500), zoom 2.2 — **KNOWN WRONG per confirmed bug above** — must be retargeted to the right-panel voice-to-text input box

For each of the 7, densely sample the actual source frames in its time window and either CONFIRM the existing crop/zoom is right, or REPLACE it with a corrected crop center + zoom level (max 2.2x) and corrected timing if the described moment happens at a different time than assumed. Also flag if any of the 7 should be DROPPED entirely (no zoom warranted) or if you spot an additional moment in these same clips that deserves a zoom but wasn't caught.

Return ONLY a JSON array (no prose, no markdown fences), one entry per zoom you recommend (corrected or newly added), using this shape — note "rd" is the ramp-in duration in seconds (keep 0.9-1.2), "rs" will be computed by the caller as (your absolute zoom start time) minus (the clip's start time i.e. 399.85, 446.83, 469.23, 636.05, 675.14, 708.08, or 744.57/769.35 respectively) so just give absolute source-video seconds for zoom_start:

[{"clip_start": 446.83, "zoom_start": 448.0, "cx": 954, "cy": 813, "zoom": 2.0, "target_desc": "...", "confirmed_or_corrected": "confirmed|corrected|dropped|new"}, ...]

End with one plain-text line summarizing what changed vs the original 7.
